next_smallest_discriminating_cut.claim_boundary: Still an exploratory conditional operand effect; do not call it a first writer or semantic restoration without cross-boundary and semantic-consumer evidence.
next_smallest_discriminating_cut.purpose: Separate a reproducible recipient-conditioned A/M trend from a single-boundary downstream response while avoiding a broad new grid.
next_smallest_discriminating_cut.recommendation: Repeat the same 2x2 A/M factorial at one adjacent pre-block boundary with R fixed to 0, retaining changed text and the same C reset, then compare the sign/magnitude trajectory through the next native block suffix. Add the R=1 rows only if the R=0 contrast changes materially.

limitations: Eleven dependent native futures share one observed shape contrast; prior coarse outcomes informed selection and controls.
p and factorial coefficients describe signed final-latent geometry, not semantic operations, sphere scores or independent image forecasts.
Source ports and shared native projection outputs were observed; the publisher does not reevaluate weights, attention or diffusion.
All masks and failed controls remain in the publication. Undefined p leaves affected coefficients undefined.
Full image state is edited; there is no discovered object mask, first-writer localization or minimal semantic circuit claim.
MLP operands are never removed; small replacement effects do not establish negligible or unnecessary native MLP computation.
Post-block recipient working text is fixed across masks and available for within-step1 reconstruction; only persistent conditioning is reset atstep2.
Both frozen numerical rank directions match; broad M-only sphere/RA mixed visual guesses are consistent but not exact image forecasts.
Opposite signed M effects across residual surfaces are posthoc conditional observations, not a discovered semantic operation.

The same supplied M operand does not mean an identical installed BF16 local increment: highly aligned measured deltas differ across R/A contexts. This does not isolate rounding from downstream nonlinear amplification as the explanation of final sign reversal.

local_M_geometry.interpretation: The real-arithmetic local law is additive at fixed gate. Native BF16 projection/residual rounding makes installed deltas context dependent too; these comparisons do not isolate rounding versus downstream nonlinear amplification as the cause of final sign reversal.
local_M_geometry.scope: Actual installed image differences from saved typed cuts, in float64 diagnostic arithmetic. No projection, native model, suffix or VAE executes.
local_M_geometry.source_M_operand: The same saved native base M operand is substituted in every M=1 arm.

hypotheses.H-A-vs-M: Tentative extrapolation: attention-only replacement moves farther baseward than MLP-only: p010 < p001. This is not a semantic law or gate.
hypotheses.H-RA-rank: Tentative extrapolation from earlier relation work: final latent p(merge.110) < min(p(merge.100), p(merge.010)), with base=0 and changed=1. All misses remain observations.
hypotheses.H-controls: copy.sham and merge.000 exactly reproduce changed; merge.111 reconstructs base image at exit while retaining changed text, so it reproduces the coarse after_single4.restore_image, not native base.
hypotheses.H-limits: This tests conditional operand effects at one overlap boundary; it does not identify the first or minimal shape writer. Fixed recipient MLP or attention can still be essential to later computation.
hypotheses.H-replay: Both references exactly reproduce coarse reference PNGs under common base conditioning from step2.
hypotheses.H-shape: MLP-only is predicted to retain the red sphere; RA is predicted to produce a cube-like or mixed red object. Record uncertainty, ordering, blue shape, scale and palette separately.

limits: Qualitative observations by one assistant, not calibrated human annotation or terminal shape certification.
The observer knows the task's shape hypothesis and previous experiments, but not the randomized arm identities or this run's numeric outcomes at annotation time.
Glossy reflections and soft edges can make a rounded cuboid look spherical or make a sphere look faceted; A and I remain mixed/uncertain rather than forced into a binary category.
No pixel equality, exact three-dimensional geometry, material identity, causal necessity, independent-replication or universal-rule claim is made.
Visible pose, scale and palette notes are descriptive, not calibrated measurements. Nearly indistinguishable sphere-like images are not ranked by subtle differences.
No model runs, native replays, equation evaluations, semantic evaluator calls or image edits were performed.
